papers.title: Superspecial curves of genus two over prime fields: Frobenius types and rational (2,2)-kernels
papers.abstract: Superspecial curves of genus two over a prime field $\mathbb{F}_p$, and the rational $(2,2)$-isogenies between their Jacobians, are the vertices and edges of the graph on which genus-two isogeny-based cryptography is built. Let $C$ be such a curve, with Jacobian $J$ and Frobenius endomorphism $\pi$. We show that $\pi^2 = p\,\alpha_*$ for a unique automorphism $\alpha$ of $C$ over $\mathbb{F}_p$ whose action on the Weierstrass points is the square of that of Frobenius. For $p \ge 7$ this gives the list of Frobenius types of the Weierstrass points: eight types, each with its Weil polynomial, a congruence condition on $p$, and its number 15, 3, 3, 7, 1, 1, 3 or 1 of $\mathbb{F}_p$-rational $(2,2)$-kernels; when all Weierstrass points are rational, the 2-Tate pairing on $J[2]$ is determined by $p \bmod 8$. We then prove closed formulas, in terms of class numbers of imaginary quadratic orders and of $\zeta_{\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt p)}(-1)$, for the mass of the curves of each type and for the mass of the rational kernels whose quotient is a product of elliptic curves. For $\pi^2 = \pm p$ the total masses are due to Ibukiyama and to Xue and Yu; our proofs use the 2-adic Tate modules, the symmetry of the Richelot correspondence and Eichler's mass formula, and, for the other curves, modules over orders of a quartic CM field. The kernels are counted through gluings of supersingular elliptic curves. As a consequence, the proportion of rational kernels with decomposed quotient is of order $p^{-1/2}(1+L(1,\chi))$, where $\chi$ is the quadratic character of $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-p})$. All formulas agree with an exact enumeration for the 37 primes $7 \le p \le 173$. Finally we describe the graph of $\mathbb{F}_p$-rational Richelot isogenies, which is far from connected in the range computed, and discuss what these results say about its use in isogeny-based cryptography.

papers.title: Semifields and rank-metric codes from Drinfeld modules
papers.abstract: We establish a connection between Drinfeld modules and rank-metric codes, focusing on maximum rank distance codes arising from finite semifields. Our method constructs rank-metric codes from linear subspaces of endomorphisms of a Drinfeld module acting on torsion submodules. Using a duality between a Drinfeld module and its endomorphisms, we show that Sheekey's construction fits naturally into this framework, yielding a short conceptual proof of his main theorem. Next, to demonstrate the potential of our method, we construct, for every prime power $q$, new semifields of order $q^9$, which are distinguished from the known ones by their nuclear parameters. Finally, going beyond the Drinfeld module $\phi_T=\tau^n$ that underlies Sheekey's and related constructions, we obtain infinite families of semifield codes from Drinfeld modules with smaller endomorphism rings, and show that the corresponding semifields are cyclic semifields of Petit.

papers.title: Heights and energies of polarized fibrations of varieties
papers.abstract: We study nef line bundles on polarized fibrations $(X/C,\bar{H})$, with a fixed nef metrized ample polarization satisfying $H^d=1$, where $d=\dim X$. We prove a quantitative arithmetic height inequality under relative metric positivity, allowing singular arithmetic models and relatively nef adelic bundles. The height deficit defines a local energy. For nef, relatively ample line bundles over finitely generated fields, this energy is bounded below for almost every complex or nonarchimedean local-field realization of fixed polarized global model data, outside one null set common to the entire relative metric class. The results include big non-semiample examples. For ample $L$ and smooth positively curved $\bar{H}$, the complex critical equation is the Calabi--Yau equation; at zero volume, projective bundles recover Donaldson's functional. We also study critical metrics and conjectural canonical heights defined by energy envelopes.

papers.title: The Ceresa Cycle on $X_0^+(p)$
papers.abstract: We consider the curve $X_0^+(p)$ with prime $p$, which is the quotient of the modular curve $X_0(p)$ by the Fricke involution. We describe how one can explicitly calculate the shadow of a Hecke operator on $X_0^+(p)$, which is a rational divisor on $X_0^+(p)$ whose nonvanishing is an obstruction to the Ceresa cycle of $X_0^+(p)$ being torsion in the Chow group of the Jacobian of $X_0^+(p)$. We also provide an implementation of this procedure in PARI/GP and SageMath and use this on all primes below 5000.

papers.title: Irreducible components of affine Deligne-Lusztig variety in the affine flag variety
papers.abstract: We establish a bijection between elements of stable Demazure crystals and labeled longest increasing paths in the double Bruhat graph. As an application, we show that the orbits of irreducible components of certain special affine Deligne-Lusztig varieties (ADLVs) in the affine flag variety of a split reductive group are counted by weight multiplicities of the associated Demazure modules for the dual group. By decomposing an arbitrary ADLV into strata that are iterated fibrations over these special ADLVs, we then obtain a formula for the number of orbits of irreducible components for ADLVs in the affine flag variety, generalizing the numerical form of the Chen-Zhu conjecture.

papers.title: Optimal homological stability: bounding secondary terms of Cohen-Lenstra moments and $S_d$-fields over $\mathbb{F}_q[t]$
papers.abstract: We prove an explicit stability line for the homology $H_i(\mathrm{Hur}_n^c,\mathbb{Q})$ of any Hurwitz space associated to a finite rack $c$ depending only on its homology up to some finite $n$. Moreover, as the range of $n$ increases, the slope of the resulting stability line converges to the optimal slope. Thus, for any Hurwitz space, a finite computation will yield near-optimal bounds on secondary terms for the corresponding arithmetic statistics problem. Our theorem also applies more generally to higher order stability, Frobenius weights, and braided vector spaces. As a special case of our theorem, we can deduce stability lines depending only on when $H_0(\mathrm{Hur}^c_n,\mathbb{Q})$ stabilizes, which are sharp in some cases. We apply this to two families of Hurwitz spaces to obtain bounds on the secondary term for (1) the number of $S_d$-degree $d$ function fields with squarefree discriminant, and (2) Cohen-Lenstra moments.

papers.title: Bernstein-Zelevinsky duality for equivariant vector bundles on Drinfeld spaces
papers.abstract: We study duality and finiteness of locally analytic representations arising from compactly supported coherent cohomology of Drinfeld spaces. We prove that Grothendieck--Serre duality for equivariant vector bundles realizes Bernstein--Zelevinsky duality of locally analytic representations. We follow the strategy of Fargues for $\ell$-adic sheaves and obtain resolutions of locally analytic representations by compactly induced representations. The resolutions motivate us to introduce the notion of locally analytic representations of compact presentation, which generalizes the notion of finitely presented representations. These representations are related to prim objects on the classifying stack in the sense of $6$-functor formalism and their extension groups to admissible locally analytic representations are finite-dimensional. As an application, we establish Serre duality for extension groups of locally analytic representations of $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{Q}_p)$ attached to non-trianguline de Rham Galois representations under the $p$-adic local Langlands correspondence.

papers.title: Supersingular Ekedahl-Oort strata and Oort's conjecture
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{A}_g$ be the moduli space over $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p$ of $g$-dimensional principally polarised abelian varieties, where $p$ is a prime. We show that if $g$ is even and $p\geq 5$, then every geometric generic member in the maximal supersingular Ekedahl-Oort stratum in $\mathcal{A}_g$ has automorphism group $\{ \pm 1\}$. This confirms Oort's conjecture in the case of $p\geq 5$ and even $g$. We also separately prove Oort's conjecture for $g=4$ and $p >2$.

papers.title: Irreducible $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$-action on projective $k$-lattices and Frobenius numbers
papers.abstract: The irreducible representation of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ induces an action on the space $X_k(\mathbb{R}^n)$ of projective classes of rank $k$-discrete subgroups in $\mathbb{R}^n$. For every lattice subgroup of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ and every starting point in $X_k(\mathbb{R}^n)$ and $2\leq k<n$, we prove convergence of the orbit averages over expanding norm balls and give a complete, explicit description of their limits. In an overview, every limit is supported on the subbundle over the unique compact $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$-orbit in the Grassmannian. The conditional measures on the fibers are either uniform on finite sets or convex combinations of at most two homogeneous measures associated with split simple subgroups of $\mathrm{PGL}_k(\mathbb{R})$ containing the principal $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$. Another objective of our work is to relate weak-$*$ limits of probability measures on $X_{n-1}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ supported on the projective classes of lattices orthogonal to integer vectors with limiting distributions of the corresponding normalized Frobenius numbers. This correspondence gives limit laws for vectors sampled from certain proper subvarieties, extending J. Marklof's work on sampling from full-dimensional domains. Specifically, together with our results for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ orbits in $X_{n-1}(\mathbb{R}^n)$, this correspondence gives limit laws for primitive integer vectors sampled from $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$-orbits. Using an earlier result of the first author and Shapira, we obtain analogous laws for integer vectors sampled on level sets of certain quadratic forms, as the level tends to infinity.

papers.title: Incidence methods for algebraic expanders over arbitrary fields
papers.abstract: Let $A\subset F$ be finite, $N=|A|$, $p=\operatorname{char}F$ (with $p=\infty$ in characteristic zero), and $L=1+\log(2N)$. In the range $N\le p^{1/2}$, we establish \[ |AA+A|\gg N^{129/85}L^{-72/85}. \] This improves the long-standing $3/2$-exponent bound for $AA+A$ in positive characteristic in the range $N\le p^{1/2}$, without any assumption on the multiplicative doubling of $A$. We further establish uniform expansion bounds with exponents $129/85$ and $32/21$ for four families of three-variable product--quotient expanders, together with refined estimates over prime fields. For $\lambda\in F^\times$ and $N\le p^{1/2}$, our four-variable bounds include \[ |AA+\lambda AA|\gg N^{214/135}L^{-7/9},\qquad |AA-AA|\gg_\varepsilon N^{6681/4175-\varepsilon} \quad(\varepsilon>0). \] In particular, several three- and four-variable targets admit uniform lower bounds with exponents greater than $3/2$ in the large-characteristic range. We also prove bounds with exponent $49/38$ for shifted products and shifted quotients, and for quadratic-image sumsets when $\operatorname{char}F\ne 2$, as well as characteristic-sensitive estimates for $AA+\lambda A/A$ and $(A-A)^\times/(A-A)^\times$. The proofs combine higher-energy inequalities, regularisation, and point--line incidences.

papers.title: Asymptotics for generalized integer partitions
papers.abstract: We study the asymptotic behavior of weighted partition functions $p_f(n)$, defined by the generating function $\prod_{n \geq 1} (1 - q^{n})^{-f(n)}$ with non-negative real weights $f(n)$. We assume that the associated Dirichlet series $D(s) = \sum_{n \geq 1} f(n) n^{-s}$ admits a meromorphic continuation to a half-plane $\Re(s) \geq -\varepsilon$, with finitely many real poles of arbitrary orders, the largest of which is a positive pole $\alpha$ of order $k$, and a possibly infinite collection of complex poles lying strictly to the left of $\alpha$, with some additional conditions. We extend the saddle-point method of Debruyne and Tenenbaum, and show that the pole $\alpha$ dominates the contribution of all other poles. As a result, we give an explicit asymptotic formula for $p_f(n)$ described via generalized Lambert functions. Furthermore, we show that for $k \geq 2$ no finite combination of powers of $n$, $\log n$, $\log \log n, \ldots$ approximates the saddle point well enough to give an asymptotic formula for $p_f(n)$. We also discuss a number of applications related to algebra, number theory, and combinatorics.

papers.title: A disproof of the van Emde Boas--Kruyswijk conjecture on the Davenport constant
papers.abstract: The Davenport constant $D(G)$ of a finite abelian group $G$ is the smallest positive integer $\ell$ such that every sequence $S$ with terms from $G$ and with length $|S| \ge \ell$ has a nontrivial zero-sum subsequence. A long-standing conjecture, first proposed by van Emde Boas and Kruyswijk in 1969, states that $D(C_n^r)=r(n-1)+1$ for all positive integers $n$ and $r$. In this paper, we disprove this conjecture by showing that $D(C_6^r)>5r+1$ for every $r\ge23$.

papers.title: Divisibility of Character Values of Wreath Products of Symmetric Groups
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a finite group whose character table is integer-valued, and let $K$ be any fixed positive integer. We prove that almost every entry of the character table of the wreath product $G\wr S_N$ is divisible by $K$ as $N\to\infty$.

papers.title: Low Moments, Small Balls and Star Discrepancy
papers.abstract: Let $D_P$ be the discrepancy function of a configuration $P$ of $N$ points in the $d$-dimensional unit cube, and let $\|D_P\|_q$ be its $L^q$ discrepancy. We prove that for all fixed $d\ge2$ and $0<q\le1$ the $L^q$ discrepancy of every configuration of $N\ge2$ points is at least $c_{d,q}(\log N)^{(d-1)/2}$ with a constant $c_{d,q}>0$. This bound is sharp; together with the classical results for $q>1$, it determines the minimal order of the $L^q$ discrepancy for every $0<q<\infty$ in every dimension $d\ge2$, and for $q=1$ it answers Chen's problem on the sharp lower bound for the $L^1$ discrepancy in dimension $d\ge3$. We prove the small ball inequality for Haar functions in every fixed dimension $d\ge3$ and for arbitrary real coefficients with the conjectured power of $n$, up to a polylogarithmic factor; here $2^{-n}$ is the smallest volume of the dyadic boxes involved. The method also extends to a class of piecewise polynomial mother functions. For the $L^\infty$ discrepancy $\|D_P\|_\infty=ND^*(P)$, where $D^*(P)$ is the star discrepancy, we prove the conjectured lower bound $c(\log N)^{3/2}$ in dimension three, and the lower bound $(\log N)^{d/2}$ up to a power of $\log\log N$ in every fixed dimension $d\ge4$. Finally, we construct $N$-point sets whose $L^\infty$ discrepancy is $O_d((\log N)^{d-1-1/16})$ in every fixed dimension $d\ge3$; this disproves the conjectured optimality of the order $(\log N)^{d-1}$ of the classical constructions.

papers.title: Narrower arithmetic progressions in the primes
papers.abstract: For each fixed $k\geq 3$ and $\delta > 0$, we prove that every subset of the primes up to $X$ of relative density at least $\delta$ contains a non-trivial $k$-term arithmetic progression with common difference $O_{k,\delta,\varepsilon}((\log X)^{k\cdot 2^{k-3}+\varepsilon})$, for any $\varepsilon>0$. This improves the previous exponent $(k-1)2^{k-2}$. The main ingredient is a relative Szemer\'{e}di theorem for narrow progressions under weaker linear forms conditions.

papers.title: An Explicit Uniform Connectivity Bound for Generalized Markoff Graphs
papers.abstract: Let $X_D$ be the surface $x^2+y^2+z^2-xyz=D$ over $\mathbb F_p$. For every prime $p>10^{320}$ and every $D\in\mathbb F_p\setminus\{4\}$, we prove that the three Vieta involutions act transitively on the trace triples of generating pairs of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb F_p)$. The proof combines an explicit primitive-fiber argument, Chen's orbit-size lower bound, and a weighted maximal-divisor estimate. We also give an explicit descent from Nielsen transitivity to transitivity under the Vieta involutions alone.

papers.title: Nine-Colored Partition Components Modulo 19
papers.abstract: Let $p_{m}(n)$ be the number of partitions of $n$ into parts of $m$ colors, and let $y=q^{19}$. Starting from Winquist's identity, as Hirschhorn did for the modulus $11$, we express each of the nineteen components of $(q;q)_{\infty}^{10}$ modulo $19$ as a sum of two quartic products of the theta functions $(y^{a};y^{19})_{\infty}(y^{19-a};y^{19})_{\infty}$, and deduce all nineteen generating functions $\sum_{n} p_{9}(19n+r)y^{n}$ modulo $19$ in closed form. The vanishing class $p_{9}(19n+17)$ is the one known previously. For seventeen colors, the residue class singled out by Kiming and Olsson carries no congruence, and we show that its generating function is $y f(y^{19})^{2}/f(y)$ modulo $19$. Along the way, we recall, with proofs, such exact relationships known for all these congruences. O'Brien's cubic relation is a Weierstrass equation for $X_{0}(19)$ in Kolberg's coordinates; we prove the existence of a doubling automorphism of the theta functions, fixing the cubic, which acts on both dissections by explicit scalars. All proofs are by hand.

papers.title: Cameron--Martin theorem for SLE welding measures
papers.abstract: For $\kappa\in(0,4]$, we prove a Cameron--Martin theorem for the welding law induced by SLE$_\kappa$ loop measure. Under simultaneous left and right composition $h\mapsto\varphi\circ h\circ\psi^{-1}$, the transformed law is mutually absolutely continuous with respect to the original law exactly when both maps belong to the Weil--Petersson group, and is mutually singular otherwise. Thus the Weil--Petersson group is the quasi-invariance group of the welding law under composition on either side. We also prove that it is its own normalizer in the group of orientation-preserving circle homeomorphisms. For Weil--Petersson pairs, we derive an explicit Radon--Nikodym derivative in terms of a relative action well defined for SLE weldings and prove that it belongs to $L^{1+\varepsilon}$ for some $\varepsilon>0$ depending on the pair.

papers.title: Nahm Sums Dual to Zagier's Rank Three Examples and Related Identities
papers.abstract: In 2007, Zagier identified twelve families of candidates for rank three modular Nahm sums and established the modularity of three of them. The remaining cases were subsequently confirmed by Wang. Zagier's duality observation indicates that the Nahm sums associated with the duals of these examples might still be modular. We confirm that this is indeed true. The modularity of the dual of the sixth example was previously established by Milas and Wang, while that of the dual of the eleventh example was partially established by Shi and Wang. We settle all remaining cases, thereby establishing the modularity of every defined dual in Zagier's rank three list. We achieve this by proving new Rogers--Ramanujan type identities that express the relevant Nahm sums as finite sums of infinite products. Along the way we discover two new families of modular rank three Nahm sums. As applications, we prove some Nahm sum identities conjectured by Cao--Wang, Shi--Wang and Li.

papers.title: New lower bounds for even and odd values of the partition function
papers.abstract: Let $N_{\mathrm{odd}}(X)$ and $N_{\mathrm{even}}(X)$ denote the numbers of integers $0\leq n\leq X$ for which the ordinary partition function $p(n)$ is odd and even, respectively. The Parkin--Shanks conjecture predicts that $N_{\mathrm{odd}}(X)$ and $N_{\mathrm{even}}(X)$ are both asymptotic to $X/2$. Bella\"iche and Nicolas proved that $N_{\mathrm{even}}(X)\gg \sqrt{X} \log \log X$, while Zheng, building on work of Ono and Swaminathan, recently proved that $N_{\mathrm{odd}}(X)\gg \sqrt{X}$. We improve both bounds simultaneously by proving $\min\{N_{\mathrm{odd}}(X), N_{\mathrm{even}}(X)\}\gg X^{3/4}/(\log X \log \log X)$. These results have been verified formally in Lean by AxiomProver.

papers.title: On the $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear relations among multiple zeta values in positive characteristic
papers.abstract: This paper gives a new path to determine all $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear relations among multiple zeta values in positive characteristic, which had been done by Huang, Lai, Li and the author. The path used in this paper is based on the idea of operator generation, which originated from the work of Todd, developed by the author, and independently by Im-Kim-Ngo Dac.

papers.title: On counting integer symmetric matrices of fixed determinant in families of slant boxes
papers.abstract: In this article, we develop an upper bound for the number of integral symmetric matrices of fixed determinant in a slant box with coefficients bounded by some given power of the volume of the slant box. We develop a counting method that expands on Shankar-Siad-Swaminathan's work on rank-3 integer symmetric matrices of fixed determinant to higher-rank matrices using geometry-of-numbers methods and invariant theory on the splitting of quadratic forms associated with the determinant formula into corresponding linear forms. We expect this generalization will allow us to apply the counting results to arithmetic statistics frameworks. In forthcoming work, we will apply the counting results to study the distribution of 2-torsion subgroups of class groups of unit-monogenised number fields.

papers.title: Zero-sum subsequences of cross number $1$ over cyclic groups
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, and let $\mathsf{T}(G)$ be the smallest integer $t$ such that every sequence of length $t$ over $G$ contains a nonempty zero-sum subsequence of cross number $1$. We determine the exact value of $\mathsf{T}(C_n)$ for every positive integer $n$, showing that $\mathsf{T}(C_n)=2n-1$ when $n$ is odd and $\mathsf{T}(C_n)=3n/2-1$ when $n$ is even. In particular, $\mathsf{T}(C_n)=\mathsf{s}(C_n)$ for odd $n$.

papers.title: Generalizing the Gaster--Loustau Theorem via Generalized Discrete Markov Spectra
papers.abstract: We realize generalized Markov numbers (GM numbers) for arbitrary $k_1,k_2,k_3\in \mathbb Z_{\ge0}$ as $\lambda$-lengths of return arcs on a hyperbolic orbifold constructed from local monodromy matrices. The McShane identity of Tan--Wong--Zhang on this orbifold yields a summation identity with multiplicities for the gaps between the associated Markov--Lagrange constants and their limiting value, together with a summation inequality that counts each distinct value once. These results extend the summation identity and inequality of Gaster and Loustau to generalized Markov numbers.

papers.title: On p-adic asymptotic formulas for slope factors of L-functions of toric exponential sums
papers.abstract: Adolphson and Sperber expressed the unique unit root of the $L$-function of a toric exponential sum in terms of $A$-hypergeometric functions, whereas reciprocal zeros and poles of positive slope remain much less understood.We study complete rational factors of arbitrary prescribed slope in families satisfying a chain-level ordinary condition. Our main tool is a new contraction map arising from a twisted block LU factorization of the Frobenius matrix of a nuclear $\sigma$-module. Its fixed point produces an upper triangularization and the associated slope filtration, while explicit Schur-complement quotients of finite Frobenius iterates approximate the diagonal slope blocks with geometrically decreasing error. At a periodic fiber, successive cancellation in an ordered product of these approximations yields a quotient formed from two finite Frobenius iterates, and the characteristic polynomial of this quotient converges to the complete slope polynomial. Combined with the relative Dwork trace formula, this yields uniform $p$-adic asymptotic formulas for the complete slope factors of the $L$-functions of toric exponential sums. When the relevant slope blocks have rank one, the Schur complements reduce to ratios of leading principal minors and give asymptotic formulas for the individual reciprocal zeros and poles after cancellation.

papers.title: The inverse Littlewood problem for multiplicative functions
papers.abstract: We formulate and solve the asymptotic inverse Littlewood problem in the class of multiplicative functions. That is, let $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{U}\cup\{0\}$ be a bounded completely multiplicative function satisfying $\sum_{p:f(p)=0}1/p<\infty$. We show that \[ \int_0^1 \left|\sum_{n\le x}f(n)e(\alpha n)\right|\,d\alpha\ll\log x \] for all $x\ge3$ if and only if $f(n)=\chi(n)n^{it}$ for some Dirichlet character $\chi$ and some $t\in\mathbb{R}$.\\ More generally, we show that there is $\varepsilon_0>0$, depending only on the $\ell^2$-density of $f$ (that is, on $\prod_{p:f(p)=0}(1-1/p)$), such that under the weaker hypothesis \[ \int_0^1 \left|\sum_{n\le x}f(n)e(\alpha n)\right|\,d\alpha \ll x^{\varepsilon_0} \] for all $x\ge3$, there are a Dirichlet character $\chi$ and $t\in\mathbb{R}$ such that \[ \sum_p\frac{\left|f(p)-\chi(p)p^{it}\right|}{p}<\infty. \] We give evidence for the sharpness of such classification, by constructing non-pretentious examples with $L^1$ norm $o(\sqrt{x})$ at every sufficiently large scale, but with ``wild" behavior at the intermediate scales.

papers.title: Cyclic Self-Dual Codes over Prime-Square Rings and Unimodular Lattices
papers.abstract: We present an explicit construction of cyclic Euclidean self-dual codes over $\mathbb{Z}/p^{2}\mathbb{Z}$, where $p$ is an odd prime, and use Construction~A to obtain unimodular lattices with large minimum norms. The construction is based on reciprocal factorizations of $x^n-1$. We explicitly describe the associated residue and torsion codes and analyze the relationship between minimum Euclidean weights and lattice minimum norms. We construct a unimodular lattice of minimum norm~$4$ in dimension~$49$, unimodular lattices of minimum norm~$5$ in dimensions $53$, $55$, $58$, $59$, and~$61$, and extremal unimodular lattices of minimum norm~$6$ in dimensions $69$ and~$71$. Using shadow theory and harmonic theta series, we prove that extremal unimodular lattices do not exist in dimensions $59$ and~$61$. Together with the known upper bounds, these results establish the optimality of the constructed lattices in all eight dimensions. In particular, we determine the previously unknown optimal minimum norms of unimodular lattices in five dimensions: $53$, $55$, $61$, $69$, and~$71$. We further construct unimodular lattices whose minimum norms are exactly one below the corresponding extremal bounds in dimensions $62$, $63$, $65$, $67$, $70$, $89$, $91$, $92$, $93$, and~$94$.

papers.title: 44 Tropen by Josef Matthias Hauer as orbits under the group of interval shifts
papers.abstract: We generate a splitting of the 924 monotonically ascending twelve tone half series H=(H_1,..,H_6) in [0,..,11]^6 in 80 orbits H^G under the additive cyclic group G=Z/12Z of transpositions (interval shifts). By classification according to cardinality and forming the union of the orbits H^G and K^G of a half series H and its complement K, we obtain exactly the 44 Tropen by Josef Matthias Hauer, completely independent of symmetry properties, however, fundamentally due to so-called wider-gleiche orbits. This was not clear in previous literature.

papers.title: One more curious property of $1729$: The only Carmichael number of the form $2^np^3+1$ with prime $p$
papers.abstract: Florian Luca recently proved that if $2^np^3+1$ is a Carmichael number for some prime $p$ and integer $n\ge1$, then $p=3$. Here we complete the cubic classification by proving that $1729$, Hardy--Ramanujan taxicab number, is the only Carmichael number of the form $2^np^3+1$ with $p$ prime and $n\ge1$. The proof identifies the unique possible multiplicatively dependent prime factor, sharpens the known bound on Fermat prime factors of $2^nk+1$ from $k^2$ to $2k$, derives the explicit bound $n\le2742$, and concludes with a short sieve requiring neither factorisation nor primality testing.

papers.title: Finding four vertices of a square of area $n$ in a grid by geometric construction
papers.abstract: In this study, we consider geometric construction in an infinite square grid. Our purpose is to find efficient methods for constructing a square of area $n\in\mathbb{N}$ based on arithmetic properties of the sum of squares. As a consequence, for each $n\in\mathbb{N}$, we derive the optimal number of construction steps required to determine the four vertices of the square. Furthermore, we classify all positive integers into three classes according to these optimal numbers.
